_comment_split: SPLIT from the monolithic S10.json (2026-08-30, ralph/T2-S10-COST). See S10a.json's header for the full rationale. This is the SECOND of five sub-segments: the chapter's climax (the Warden fight), the legendary chamber, and the release ceremony -- the single most combat-dense block in the chapter, isolated into its own segment so a fight's own price spike cannot get charged against unrelated content ahead of it (which is exactly the mechanism that blocked the original monolithic S10 at step 26: a patrol fight repriced the scene to 0.097 s/frame and that price was then applied to the REMAINING 413,884 frames of a segment that still had the giant post-win walk-back ahead of it).
_comment_boundary: Entry: seeded from S10a-exit (elite just beaten). Ends at 'the roster is settled' (original step S10-88), immediately before the walk-back objective is tracked. Frame budget at the worst MEASURED per-frame rate from the blocked run (0.097118 s/frame) is roughly 30,420 frames * 0.097 = ~2,951 s, 20% of the 14,400 s ceiling. Even at a hypothetically much worse combat cost for the single hardest fight in the game (0.2 s/frame, double the worst measured rate) this segment prices at ~6,084 s, 42% of ceiling -- comfortable margin either way.

args.text: This is the SECOND of S10's five split sub-segments (S10a..S10e; see S10a.json's header). Its entry save is `S10a-exit`, a split-introduced handoff (the elite freshly beaten, shutter lifted) rather than one section B names in the original monolithic file. The three steps below are the standard handoff mechanics used at every S0n boundary: wipe, seed, boot, Load.

That finding is already captured in full, un-answered, in S02-superseded-2/3/4 and S02/BLOCKER.md -- three press counts, identical 7201-frame holds. What it buys is everything downstream: measured in S03 and S04, an unanswered modal at a walk's end left input_context='narrative_modal' where the next step expected combat, so no fight started, no catch resolved, the team never reached three, and every tournament entry check then failed on team size. steps.title: Section B save handoff

args.text: This is a SPLIT-introduced handoff point -- the roster ceremony has just concluded, a quiet state. The steps below save it, driven as a player drives it -- the pause shell (opened via the `map` shortcut, RIG-14's deterministic starting point), three RB presses to the Save tab, focus down to slot 4, and the slot's own Save button. `save_out` afterwards only copies the artefact; it saves nothing itself.
